(4) EFTA02389172: Michael Harrigan (USVI Deputy Superintendent of Schools) wrote O-1B letter crediting her work through Enhanced Education on STEM competition. This system of coordinated visa letters from high-profile individuals corroborates Al Jazeera/OCCRP reporting (Feb 2026) that Rod-Larsen wrote official visa recommendation letters for women connected to Epstein.

curation.lead:
The International Peace Institute (IPI) is a New York-based international policy think tank headquartered at 777 United Nations Plaza, tracing its origins to the Trygve Lie Center for Peace, Security and Development. Registered as a 501(c)(3) with EIN 03-0213226, IPI historically operated on annual revenues exceeding $11 million, funded by Scandinavian governments (Norway and Sweden were described in IPI internal correspondence as "donor countries" [EFTA02675352]), the Gates Foundation, the Open Society Foundations, and private philanthropists [Finding #1182, #241]. Under the two-decade presidency of Norwegian diplomat Terje Rod-Larsen, the records show IPI maintaining advisory boards that included sitting US Congressional members, former heads of state, and foreign ministers, situating the institute between the United Nations diplomatic community and Western political establishments [Finding #1147].

Records released in DOJ Volume 11 and a December 2020 KPMG forensic review commissioned by IPI show that Jeffrey Epstein held a role at IPI that extended beyond philanthropy into donor liaison and fundraising intermediation. KPMG confirmed five donations totaling $650,000 from Epstein-controlled entities Enhanced Education and Gratitude America Ltd between 2011 and 2019, with a further $14,158.88 flight reimbursement for Lawrence Summers, and all Gratitude America checks drawn on Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas [Finding #69, #90]. In May 2012, IPI publicly launched a "Distinguished Fund" naming Epstein as founding philanthropist, four years after his 2008 Florida conviction [Finding #75, EFTA02721041]. In June 2013, Epstein forwarded IPI bank wiring instructions to Boris Nikolic, Bill Gates's science advisor, with the note "These are the wiring instructions for the 5 million from the foundatoin. for IPI" [Finding #73, EFTA02707935]. The Gates Foundation subsequently awarded a $2.5 million grant (OPP1096058) signed March 2014, following a full-day negotiation meeting at the Gates campus attended by Nikolic [Finding #237, #238]. Leon Black separately donated $200,000 in December 2014, a contribution tracked by Epstein's accountant Richard Kahn alongside Black's other Epstein-directed charitable giving [Finding #80, EFTA02465679]. Investigators working from DOJ files estimate that Epstein's intermediation was connected to roughly $5.86 million in funding reaching IPI [Finding #93, synthesis].

IPI's financial trajectory after the Epstein relationship became public tracks the institutional cost of that dependency. An analysis of the 990 filings shows revenue peaking at $11.87 million in 2014 and declining steadily to $3.93 million in 2020, the year Rod-Larsen resigned and the KPMG review was commissioned, with assets falling from $16.37 million (2014) to $6.91 million (2023) [Finding #241, #87, 990:030213226]. Across the same filings, expenses exceeded revenue in every year except 2010 and 2021, a pattern the review of the records reads as reserve draw-down [Finding #423, #458]. In December 2022, a qui tam (False Claims Act) whistleblower lawsuit was filed against IPI in the District of Minnesota, Case No. 0:22-cv-03127 before Judge Jeffrey M. Bryan [Finding #240]. IPI carries zero FARA or LDA registrations despite foreign government donor inflows and Congressional advisory programming, a posture that, on examination of the FARA record, is anomalous relative to peer Norwegian-funded entities that did register [Finding #1147, synthesis].
curation.system_role: On the evidence in DOJ Volume 11 and the KPMG review, IPI operated as a UN-adjacent institutional platform through which Epstein obtained diplomatic access, public legitimacy as a "philanthropist," and a channel for directing donations from figures including Leon Black and the Gates Foundation, while its Norwegian-led presidency sat at the interface of Scandinavian government funding and Epstein's private financial architecture.

sections.title: Epstein as Funding Architect
sections.content:
The DOJ Volume 11 records show Epstein acting as a fundraising intermediary and donor liaison to Rod-Larsen rather than a passive donor [Finding #82]. On January 31, 2011, Epstein wrote to Rod-Larsen that "I have bill gates for the nxt two days.. I know what i am supposed to say re IPI.. any specific challenge?" [EFTA01834272]. By April 2013 the pitch had sharpened to "get me the info on ipi, to give to bg" [EFTA01898063], and a January 2014 note from Rod-Larsen to Epstein celebrated that "the International Peace Institute (IPI), now can celebrate [X] years of cooperation with the Gates Foundation" while proposing a joint lunch at Davos [EFTA02625684].

The mechanics of the Gates relationship are unusually well-documented in the record. On June 10, 2013, Epstein forwarded IPI's JPMorgan Chase wiring instructions to Boris Nikolic with the note about "the 5 million from the foundatoin" [Finding #73, EFTA02707935]. On September 11, 2013, IPI and Gates Foundation staff held a full-day meeting at the Gates campus; the meeting agenda lists Nikolic as "Scientific Advisor" [Finding #238, EFTA02725118]. IPI had submitted a $20 million proposal for polio eradication work across Afghanistan, Pakistan, Nigeria, and Somalia [Finding #290, EFTA02678411], and the Foundation approved $2.5 million (grant OPP1096058) [Finding #237]. When the agreement was signed on March 2, 2014, Rod-Larsen forwarded the executed grant directly to Epstein [EFTA01934403]. In March 2015, when the Gates Foundation declined a second IPI pandemic-preparedness proposal, Rod-Larsen again forwarded the rejection letter to Epstein [Finding #239, EFTA02713877]. A cross-reference of the correspondence indicates Epstein served as the principal external intermediary on IPI's Gates Foundation relationship [Finding #82, synthesis].

The DOJ files also show Epstein placing IPI alongside his personal financial planning. An April 14, 2015 estate-planning email lists "charity, new trusts,!!d IPI, harvard, fees" in the same line as "estate modification given new circunstances and altered probablities" [Finding #93, HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_023273]. IPI internal correspondence further shows Rod-Larsen directing staff to send Epstein the same program activity reports "which we usually forward to donor countries like Sweden or Norway" [Finding #1182, EFTA02675352] — a level of donor-equivalent reporting that placed a registered sex offender among IPI's institutional stakeholders alongside sovereign donors.

sections.title: Financial Flows and Conduits
sections.content:
The KPMG forensic review dated December 18, 2020 identified five donations from Epstein-controlled entities totaling $650,000 [Finding #69]. Enhanced Education contributed $125,000 on October 11, 2011, designated for the "WK Rick Hooper fellowship." Gratitude America Ltd made four additional payments: $150,000 on May 8, 2017, labeled "Reimbursement of tickets to the Oslo Play"; $125,000 on June 12, 2017; $100,000 on November 1, 2017, labeled "Contribution from Gatitude [sic] America, LTD Oslo Play"; and a further $150,000 on April 5, 2019, three months before Epstein's arrest [Finding #69, #84, #90]. KPMG also identified a $14,158.88 reimbursement from Enhanced Education on March 28, 2014 for a first-class Lufthansa flight from JFK to Almaty booked for Lawrence Summers, with the ticket invoiced through Protravel International to IPI at 777 United Nations Plaza [Finding #78, EFTA02711226].

LMSBAND holds image copies of the Gratitude America checks, each drawn on Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas, the same institution that maintained Epstein's personal accounts and was later fined by NYDFS over the Epstein relationship [Finding #90, EFTA01357084, EFTA01360128, EFTA01362195]. The "Oslo Play" designations on $250,000 in 2017 payments carry their own context. The Broadway play "Oslo" by J.T. Rogers dramatized Rod-Larsen's role in the 1993 Oslo Accords, Rod-Larsen hosted a private reception before a May 5, 2017 performance [EFTA02650430], and Epstein "hired out the entire theatre for the U.N." [EFTA02650158]. KPMG recorded no donor restrictions on the contributions, so IPI could apply the funds to any purpose. Set against the gap between ticket face value and the $250,000 total, analysis of the payments suggests the "Oslo Play" line functioned as a label rather than a true earmark [Finding #71, synthesis].

Beyond the direct Epstein-entity donations, Leon Black donated $200,000 to IPI in December 2014, with the donation letter addressed to Rod-Larsen at 777 UN Plaza [Finding #80, EFTA02705181]. Epstein's accountant Richard Kahn logged the Black donation alongside other charitable giving directed by Epstein in a subject line reading "Leon 2014 year end charities along with fees 2013-2015" [EFTA02465679]. Summing the $650,000 KPMG-confirmed conduit total, the $14,158.88 flight reimbursement, the $200,000 Black donation, and the $2.5 million Gates grant (plus a further $256,968 June 2019 Gates grant for polio work), the financial flow connected to Epstein's intermediation comes to approximately $5.86 million [Finding #93, synthesis].

sections.title: Diplomatic Access Platform
sections.content:
The DOJ Volume 11 record shows IPI providing Epstein with sustained access to heads of state, foreign ministers, and the UN diplomatic community [Finding #89, synthesis]. Ministerial Working Dinners on the Middle East were co-hosted at IPI by the UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah Bin Zayed Al Nahyan and the Luxembourg Foreign Minister in September 2012 and September 2014 [EFTA02683654, EFTA02726418]. IPI hosted pandemics conferences in Geneva with global health officials [EFTA02702398, EFTA02359162]. Epstein received personal invitations to the Vienna Opera Ball through IPI's Vienna office, with IPI staff member Johanna Borstner forwarding formal invitations in 2011 [EFTA02686494, EFTA02719092]. IPI also hosted a dinner for the headmaster of Stowe School at 777 UN Plaza that Epstein attended, with the invitation relayed through Rod-Larsen's assistant Camilla Reksten-Monsen [EFTA02386639].

In May 2012, IPI publicly launched a "Distinguished Fund" naming Epstein as founding philanthropist, generating press coverage in CNBC, Reuters, and The Street four years after Epstein's 2008 Florida conviction [Finding #75, EFTA02721041]. By February 2013, IPI was being featured on Epstein's personal international website, with an associate noting "putting in info about the Intl Peace Institute etc. Are there other intl. organizations that you have worked with?" [EFTA02723098]. Read alongside the invitations and the Distinguished Fund launch, the documentary record indicates IPI served a dual function — an institutional affiliation that helped rehabilitate Epstein's public profile while giving him continuing access to diplomatic networks [Finding #89, synthesis].

sections.title: Staffing Control and Personal Exploitation
sections.content:
DOJ Volume 11 records document Epstein's operational involvement in the career trajectory of at least one IPI employee [Finding #229]. In June 2016, a woman sent her resume to Epstein asking him to forward it to "Terry and Adam Lupel, who is the current Vice-Presidnet in IPI" [EFTA02460674]. By August 2016, she was drafting emails to IPI staff for Epstein's review before sending them [EFTA02390796]. She was hired as an intern at $10-$15 per hour, then moved to a full-time position at $45,000 per year. When visa issues arose, she consulted Epstein [EFTA02492920], and when negotiating salary, she sent Epstein her offer letter for review [EFTA02539626]. On February 11, 2019, IPI Vice President Adam Lupel sent Rod-Larsen a detailed employee-costs memo about her, recommending part-time employment under Gunbat sponsorship at $50,000 per year [EFTA02629771]. Rod-Larsen forwarded the memo to Epstein [Finding #229].

In March 2018, Epstein emailed someone he addressed as "president UN," introducing the same woman with the note that she "works for Terje at iPI. She is educated (the new school) and works on water issues. Is there a way to get her involved in the water project. I will subsidize if needed" [Finding #232, EFTA02512436]. The response was "Absolutely! Let her contact me, I will arrange." When Lupel's February 2019 staffing memo moved through the chain, Epstein inserted the sexually explicit line "I wonder if it ok if I have sex with her, she is s000 sexy" before forwarding it onward [Finding #231, EFTA02630683]. The woman recognized the edit as Epstein's: "Adam would never say that" [EFTA02630033]. The pattern of subsidized employment, career-decision coordination with Epstein, and the sexualized edit of official personnel documents suggests IPI's staffing process in this instance had been folded into Epstein's personal operations [Finding #229, synthesis].

Separately, Epstein's files contain O-1 visa templates and multiple completed recommendation letters designed to secure U.S. work visas for women connected to Epstein [Finding #234, EFTA02389172, EFTA02674498, EFTA02674762]. The template (EFTA02679158) instructs drafters to include "name dropping if possible," and the portfolio includes letters from Ariane de Rothschild and David Blaine drafted in O-1 visa language to certify applicants' professional standing. February 2026 reporting by Al Jazeera and OCCRP found that Rod-Larsen personally wrote official visa recommendation letters for women connected to Epstein [Finding #234].

sections.title: Regulatory Gaps and Legal Proceedings
sections.content:
The records show IPI carrying no registrations under either the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) or the Lobbying Disclosure Act (LDA), while the DOJ files describe Norway and Sweden as IPI "donor countries" [Finding #1147, EFTA02675352]. The institute's advisory programming included sitting US Congressional members, and the same records show IPI hosting foreign government officials from the UAE, Luxembourg, and elsewhere at 777 UN Plaza [Finding #1147, EFTA02683654]. Available exemptions under 22 USC 611(d) for academic or scientific institutions, or under a historical UN affiliation, are complicated by three factors: Congressional engagement beyond academic research; Rod-Larsen's routing of IPI business to Epstein, a non-diplomatic channel [Finding #1182]; and the scale of Epstein-linked funding documented in the KPMG review [Finding #69]. By comparison, a review of the filings shows Norway's development agency NORAD registered six FARA entries through consulting firms, which indicates that Norwegian-funded entities in the US do register in other cases [Finding #1147, synthesis]. On that comparison, the absence of IPI from the FARA database reads as anomalous, not as a determination of violation.

In December 2022, a qui tam whistleblower lawsuit was filed against IPI under the False Claims Act: United States ex rel. v. International Peace Institute, Inc., Case No. 0:22-cv-03127 (D. Minn.), before Judge Jeffrey M. Bryan [Finding #240]. The docket records show the case nature code as 376 Qui Tam under 31 USC 3729(a), which in False Claims Act practice signals an allegation that IPI made false claims to the federal government, often covering grant applications or certifications; the complaint is not publicly available and as of early 2026 the case has not been terminated and likely remains under seal [Finding #91, inference]. The choice of Minnesota as venue rather than the Southern District of New York, where IPI is headquartered, suggests the relator may be based in that jurisdiction [Finding #240].

Examination of IPI's governance records shows it also maintains a dual-jurisdiction corporate structure, having incorporated in Austria as a "Verein" [Finding #91, EFTA02505644]. Legal documents related to this Austrian incorporation were sent by IPI Vienna to Rod-Larsen, who forwarded them to Epstein in April 2015 [EFTA02505644]. Against this regulatory backdrop, a cross-reference of the FARA record and the donor pattern underpins the Epstein-file reviewers' argument that IPI fits a broader "shadow lobbying" pattern in which influence activity proceeds through advisory boards, foreign-government "donor country" relationships, and direct Congressional contact without appearing on FARA or LDA rolls [Finding #1147, synthesis]. That framing is an investigator synthesis drawn from the FARA record and the donor pattern, not a regulatory finding.

sections.title: Financial Collapse and Institutional Fallout
sections.content:
IPI's IRS 990 filings show a sustained financial decline that tracks the public exposure of the Epstein relationship [Finding #421, #458, 990:030213226]. Peak assets of $25.6 million in 2010 fell to $16.37 million by 2014, then continued down through $14.7 million (2015), $12.7 million (2016), $11.7 million (2017), $10.5 million (2018), and $10.4 million (2019). Following Epstein's 2019 arrest and Rod-Larsen's November 2020 resignation, reported assets moved to $7.9 million in 2020, recovered to $9.3 million in 2021, then continued down to $8.4 million (2022) and $6.91 million (2023), a 73 percent decline from the 2010 peak [Finding #421].

An analysis of the revenue figures shows a parallel trajectory [Finding #241, #87]. The $11.87 million peak in 2014, the year the Gates Foundation grant was signed, gave way to $8.47 million in 2016 and $8.39 million in 2018. The 2020 revenue figure of $3.93 million, a 67 percent drop from peak, coincided with both COVID-19 and the KPMG forensic review. The financial flow analysis shows a recovery to $10.77 million in 2021, attributed in part to a reported $1.5 million Open Society Foundations contribution tracked in LittleSis, that did not hold, with revenue falling to $6.66 million in 2022 and $5.04 million in 2023 [Finding #87, synthesis]. Expenses, by a review of the filings, exceeded revenue in every year except 2010 and 2021, pointing to the organization drawing down reserves since 2015 [Finding #423, inference].

Examination of the filings flags the 2011 990 as a separate anomaly within the series [Finding #468, inference]. Reported revenue was about $5.64 million against $13.71 million in expenses, producing an $8.07 million single-year deficit that reduced assets from $25.6 million to $17.5 million. This predates the Epstein public-exposure period, and the figure is consistent with a major investment loss, an accounting adjustment, or the departure of a significant donor, though the underlying 2011 990 PDF has not yet been re-examined. IPI employees also appear in FEC data as small-dollar ActBlue donors only, with no political giving traced to Rod-Larsen or IPI leadership [Finding #474], a pattern consistent with the Epstein relationship operating at the board and funding level rather than through staff political activity.
